questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means you:

options.text: Must slow down and be ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
Can drive through if the road is clear.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, let other vehicles and pedestrians pass first.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey over the others?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions are more important than signs, signals, and road markings. Other people authorized to direct traffic include fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: You can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle when:

options.text: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available lane to pass in.
You drive off the pavement to do it.
You are on a narrow bridge.
You can pass anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available lane to pass in.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle waiting to turn left if there is an available lane. You can also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Head restraints should be:

options.text: Set to touch the back of the head.
Removed from the seats if you can.
Set to sit above the head.
In any position—they do not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set to touch the back of the head.
questions.explanation: Set head restraints to touch the back of the head. This helps prevent injury during crashes, sudden stops, and sudden turns.

questions.question: When you see railroad tracks ahead, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains when you approach railroad tracks. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher
0.08 percent or higher
0.02 percent or higher
0.1 percent or higher

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If traffic lights stop working at an intersection:

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Let other drivers go when it is their turn. Then drive through carefully.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with siren and/or lights approaches, you must right away:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your flashers.
Stop and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights, sirens, or warning devices, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right
The vehicle coming from the left
The driver who honks first
The vehicle traveling faster

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, let a vehicle coming from the right go first.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance lets you react to problems without a hard stop, which could cause the car behind you to crash into you.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop and then go when the way is clear.
You must stop and then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop and then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before you go. Unless a sign says otherwise, this is the rule.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street with no emergency signals on. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or lights, you do not need to move. Just drive normally.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to get a ride from someone who does not drink. Coffee and cold showers do not lower your blood alcohol level. Your body needs about an hour to process one drink.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid it.
Stop right away and block its path.
Clear a path for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clear a path for the emergency vehicle to pass.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to give an emergency vehicle with flashing lights a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your car?

options.text: Put them on the back seat.
Put them on the floor near the driver's seat.
Secure them to prevent driving hazards.
Keep them on a back shelf.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them to prevent driving hazards.
questions.explanation: Secure all loose objects before driving. Objects on shelves or seats can hurt people in a crash. Objects on the floor can roll under the pedals and cause accidents.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Braking too much.
Braking suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires cannot clear water from the road. Your tires lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving uphill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may drive slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be allowed to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often drive slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. With poor visibility on hills, passing is illegal. Be careful when approaching trucks from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from:

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Enter at a low speed and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: If you need to slow down while driving on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Firmly apply your brakes.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal to slow down on a slippery road. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.
